title: 讲者态度与建议题
goal: 识别讲者本人对观点的评价；限定建议与推断的适用范围。

points.label: 识别讲者本人对观点的评价
限定建议与推断的适用范围

sources.title: 大学英语六级（CET-6）：课表
sources.used: 讲座的教学内容、知识点与练习规格

body.p: 态度题询问讲者对某一观点或做法的评价。建议题询问讲者提出的行动及其条件。讲者常先转述别人的意见，再给出自己的评价。

body.box: Some residents favor longer hours. I agree that access matters, but the cost must also be considered. If staff are available, a short trial would be useful.

body.p: 讲者同意使用机会重要，同时提出成本问题。试行的条件是有工作人员。

steps.d: 先分清观点是讲者本人的，还是讲者转述的。Some residents favor 引出居民的意见。
评价词和转折后的内容共同表示态度。agree 后的 but 引出成本方面的保留。
记录建议所依赖的条件。If staff are available 限定试行的适用情况。
would be useful 表示建议，试行尚未进行。

cards.title: 评价与立场
rows: 赞成
I support the plan because it makes access easier.
讲者支持该计划。
赞成
The proposal is worthwhile: it reduces waiting time.
讲者认可提案的价值。
质疑
I doubt the claim that a single notice reaches everyone.
讲者质疑通知覆盖所有人。
质疑
The evidence is too limited to establish that result.
讲者认为证据不足。
保留
The display is useful, although it needs regular updating.
讲者认可用途，同时指出维护需要。
保留
The plan may help, provided that enough staff are available.
有足够人员时，讲者认为计划有用。
cards.note: 评价属于说出这句话的人。让步句前后两层意思都要记下。

cards.title: 建议的条件
rows: 人员
If volunteers are available, extend the opening hours.
有志愿者时建议延长开放时间。
费用
Use the second design only if its cost remains affordable.
成本可负担是采用第二方案的条件。
时间
Before making a permanent change, test the temporary signs.
先测试临时标志，再考虑永久改变。
证据
If the sample is larger, the comparison may be more informative.
样本扩大后，比较可能更有参考价值。
cards.note: 建议说的是可以采取的行动，不是已经发生的事。may 表示可能，选项的语气不能比它强。

body.box: Some organizers say that a single notice will reach every visitor. I doubt that claim: visitors enter by different doors. If staff can update both entrances, placing a notice at each would be a sensible trial.

What does the speaker recommend?
1. Assuming that every visitor uses one door
2. Testing notices at both entrances if staff can maintain them
3. Reporting that notices have already reached every visitor
4. Removing both notices before visitors enter the building

body.p: If staff can update both entrances 限定建议的条件。placing a notice at each would be a sensible trial 对应第二项。

cards.title: 干扰项
rows: 混淆观点
The speaker believes one notice reaches everyone.
这是组织者的看法，讲者表示质疑。
遗漏条件
Place notices at both entrances regardless of staffing.
建议以工作人员能够更新为条件。
改变状态
Notices have already been placed at both entrances.
讲者提出试行，未说已经完成。
扩大程度
The trial will reach every visitor.
讲者只提出试行，没有说能通知到所有访客。

lines.text: Some staff believe a longer form is always clearer. I doubt that conclusion: adding questions can make a form harder to follow. The effect depends on which questions are added.

items.stem: What is the speaker's view of the staff's claim?
options: The speaker questions whether length always improves clarity.
The speaker agrees that every added question improves clarity.
The speaker believes that shorter forms are always the clearer ones.
The speaker says the effect depends on how many questions are added.
items.why: I doubt that conclusion 表明讲者质疑更长的表格总是更清楚，即第一项。

lines.text: The shared calendar is useful because it displays changes in one place. Still, it needs a person responsible for keeping the entries current.

items.stem: How does the speaker evaluate the calendar?
options: It is unnecessary whenever schedules change.
It is useful but requires regular maintenance.
It replaces the person who updates schedules.
It is ineffective because entries never change.
items.why: useful 和 needs a person responsible for keeping the entries current 表明肯定与保留，即第二项。

lines.text: If the room remains available in the evening, the group should test an additional meeting then. No evening meeting has been scheduled yet.

items.stem: When does the speaker recommend testing an evening meeting?
options: When the group has already scheduled every meeting
When the evening room has become unavailable
When the room can still be used in the evening
When the group has stopped meeting in the room
items.why: If the room remains available in the evening 给出试行晚间会议的条件，即第三项。

lines.text: I support making the route map available in larger print. It would help visitors who have difficulty reading the existing map. The revised map is still being prepared.

items.stem: What is the speaker's attitude toward the larger-print map?
options: The speaker doubts that the existing map is available.
The speaker believes the revised map has been distributed.
The speaker rejects the proposal because it changes the route.
The speaker favors the proposal as an aid to some visitors.
items.why: I support 和 It would help visitors 表明讲者赞成该提案，即第四项。

lines.text: Some organizers argue that a digital timetable will remove the need for printed notices. I question that conclusion because some visitors do not use the online service. A digital timetable can be useful, but printed information still serves those visitors. If staff can keep both versions current, I recommend displaying both during a trial. The trial has not yet begun, and its results should be reviewed before a permanent decision.

items.stem: What does the speaker think of replacing all printed notices?
options: The speaker doubts it, since some visitors do not use the online service.
The speaker agrees, since all visitors already use the online service.
The speaker supports it, provided that staff can keep it current.
The speaker rejects it, since digital timetables have no possible use.
items.why: I question that conclusion because some visitors do not use the online service 表明讲者质疑全部替换，即第一项。

items.stem: What condition applies to the speaker's proposed trial?
options: All visitors must agree to stop using printed notices.
Staff must be able to update both timetable formats.
The online timetable must have been permanently adopted.
The trial must already have produced its final results.
items.why: If staff can keep both versions current 是同时展示两种形式的条件，即第二项。

lines.text: Today I'd like to consider a proposal to extend the opening hours of a neighborhood repair room. The room contains shared tools and is normally staffed by volunteers. Some organizers believe that opening every evening would automatically increase participation. I question the word automatically. Longer hours can provide more opportunities, but an open room will be useful only if people know about it and can reach it. The proposal also requires people to supervise the tools and explain the rules to new visitors. I support investigating additional hours because the current schedule excludes some residents who work during the day. That potential benefit is real, even though it does not establish that opening every evening is the best choice. One option is to test a single evening each week. If enough volunteers can cover that evening for a month, I recommend a short trial. During the trial, staff could record how many people visit and what assistance they request. The record should distinguish first-time visitors from those who would otherwise have come at another time. Both groups use the room, but they tell us different things about access. A trial should also account for the work involved. Volunteers may need time to prepare the room before opening and return tools afterwards. Counting only the hours when the door is open would miss that work. Some people suggest charging a fee to cover these demands. I am not ready to endorse that idea without knowing whether a fee would prevent some residents from using the service. Cost and access should be considered together. If the trial shows demand but volunteers cannot sustain the schedule, a smaller change could be considered. For example, the room might open later on one existing day rather than add another full session. No new schedule has been adopted yet. The present recommendation is conditional: test an evening only when enough volunteers can support it, and review both participation and the effort required. A useful decision depends on those observations rather than the assumption that longer hours alone guarantee greater use.

items.stem: How does the speaker respond to the claim about opening every evening?
options: The speaker accepts that longer hours automatically increase participation.
The speaker questions whether longer hours alone guarantee greater use.
The speaker believes that the room already opens every evening.
The speaker rejects any investigation of additional opening hours.
items.why: I question the word automatically 表明讲者质疑延长时间本身保证参与人数增加，即第二项。

items.stem: What condition does the speaker attach to the proposed evening trial?
options: The trial must first show that participation has increased.
A fee must already have been adopted for all tool users.
The room must have discontinued its existing daytime schedule.
Enough volunteers must be able to staff the proposed evening.
items.why: If enough volunteers can cover that evening for a month 限定了试行条件，即第四项。

items.stem: What is the speaker's position on charging a fee?
options: The speaker withholds support until its effect on access is known.
The speaker supports a fee because it has already increased access.
The speaker proposes a fee to cover the volunteers' preparation work.
The speaker rejects any fee because it has already excluded residents.
items.why: I am not ready to endorse that idea without knowing whether a fee would prevent some residents 表明讲者暂不支持，即第一项。

lines.text: Let's examine a proposal for a local archive to provide digital copies of its photographs. Some supporters say that digitizing the collection will solve every problem of access. I doubt that a single measure can achieve that. Digital copies can help people who cannot travel to the archive, but people still need a way to find relevant images and understand what those images show. The archive also needs to maintain files over time. I favor making a selection available online, provided that the staff can describe the images accurately and maintain the files. This is support for a particular approach, not a claim that every photograph should immediately appear online. A description might identify the subject of an image and explain when the information was recorded. Where the archive is uncertain, it should indicate that uncertainty rather than present a guess as a fact. A small selection can allow the staff to test the work involved. If the archive can assign time to both description and maintenance, it should begin with one collection and review the results. The proposed selection has not yet been published. One measure of the trial would be whether visitors can find the images they need. Another would be the time staff spend correcting descriptions or replacing damaged files. The two measures concern different parts of the service. Some visitors may still prefer to consult original photographs, and some questions may require details that a particular digital image does not show clearly. An online selection can therefore complement a reading room without replacing every reason to visit. A critic has suggested that the project should be abandoned because descriptions take time. I disagree with abandoning it solely for that reason. The time required is an important cost, but it should be compared with the value of making material available to more people. If maintenance cannot be sustained, however, the archive should reduce the size of the proposed selection. The recommendation is to match the scale of publication to available staff time. The result of a small trial may help with that choice, but it cannot be treated as proof of what has already happened.

items.stem: What does the speaker think of the claim that digitization solves every access problem?
options: The speaker accepts that online images need no descriptions.
The speaker agrees, provided that the files are maintained over time.
The speaker doubts that one measure can solve all access problems.
The speaker says that digital copies cannot assist remote visitors.
items.why: I doubt that a single measure can achieve that 表明讲者质疑全面解决访问问题的说法，即第三项。

items.stem: When does the speaker recommend beginning with one collection?
options: When staff can devote time to descriptions and maintenance
When every photograph has already been published online
When visitors no longer have any reason to see originals
When visitors can already find all the images they need
items.why: If the archive can assign time to both description and maintenance 是先发布一组材料的条件，即第一项。

items.stem: What does the speaker suggest if ongoing maintenance cannot be supported?
options: Abandon the project because descriptions take time
Reduce the number of images planned for publication
Publish every image before preparing its description
Replace the reading room with an online collection
items.why: If maintenance cannot be sustained ... reduce the size of the proposed selection 对应第二项。
